author: keil
title: Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament: The Pentateuch, Vol. I (Genesis)
edition: C. F. Keil and F. Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, Vol. I: The Pentateuch, translated from the German by James Martin (Clark's Foreign Theological Library). Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark, 1866; archive.org scan "pentateuch01keil" (Princeton Theological Seminary Library), djvu OCR text
translation: Translated by the Rev. James Martin, B.A., of Nottingham (1864; this printing 1866)

rights.worldwide: to confirm: James Martin's death date (Keil died in 1888); life + 70 years

notes: The commentary on Genesis is by Keil. Keil discusses each passage as a whole and marks only some verses ("Ver. 8.", "Vers. 11, 12."), so Logia has excerpts only where he does, 218 in all. Each excerpt runs from a verse mark, up to about 350 words and cut at a sentence end. The OCR turns Keil's Hebrew into noise: a sentence holding it is left out and marked " ... ", and so is any other sentence with a word the scan prints nowhere else that is not English. Misreadings are corrected in library/corrections/keil.json only where the same scan prints the word correctly many times.
